questions.question: Who among the following is NOT a part of the Union Executive?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The Supreme Court of India.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Union executive of the government of India consists of the **President, the Vice- President, the Prime Minister, the council of ministers **and the attorney general of India.
 
• Chief Justice of India does not form a part of the Union executive.
 
• The Union executive consists of the** President, the Vice-President, and the Council of Ministers with the Prime Minister** as the head to aid and advise the President.
 
• The Chief Justice of India is the Head and Chief Judge of the Supreme Court, which consists of a maximum of **34 judges.**
 
• The Constitution requires the president to submit nominations to the Senate for its advice and consent.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The president of India is the head of state and the commander-in-chief of the Indian Armed Forces whilst the elected prime minister acts as the head of the executive and is responsible for running the Union government.
 
• Today, the prime minister is often, but not always, a member of the legislature or its lower house.
 
• According to** Article 52**, there shall be a President of India**. Article 53 **says, that the President shall be the head of the Union Executive.
 
• According to this system, there is a President who is the formal Head of the State and the Prime Minister and the Council of Ministers, which run the government at the National level.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is correct regarding the jurisdiction of the Supreme Court of India?

options.text: The original jurisdiction of the Supreme Court can be invoked by a certificate granted by the High Court.
The Supreme Court has a very wide advisory jurisdiction over all courts and tribunals in India.
The original jurisdiction extends to any dispute between the Government of India and one or more State
Article 30 of the Constitution of India gives an extensive original jurisdiction to the Supreme Court.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The original jurisdiction extends to any dispute between the Government of India and one or more State**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Supreme Court of India has original jurisdiction in any dispute between the Government of India and one or more States or between two or more States.
 
• This jurisdiction is provided under Article 131 of the Constitution of India.
 
• Original jurisdiction means the power to hear and decide cases at the first instance, rather than on appeal.
 
• The purpose of this jurisdiction is to ensure that the federal structure of the Constitution is maintained.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 131 of the Constitution of India:**

 
 
• Article 131 grants the Supreme Court original jurisdiction in any dispute between the Government of India and one or more States or between two or more States.
 
• This is a unique power as it is not shared by the High Courts or any other courts in India.
 
• This ensures that disputes of significant constitutional importance are decided by the highest court in the country.
 
 
 
• **Original Jurisdiction:**
 
 
• Original jurisdiction refers to the authority of a court to hear and decide a case for the first time, rather than reviewing a lower court's decision.
 
• In the case of the Supreme Court of India, its original jurisdiction includes matters relating to disputes between the center and states, and between states themselves.
 
 
 
• **Advisory Jurisdiction:**
 
 
• Advisory jurisdiction refers to the power of the Supreme Court to give advice to the President of India on legal or constitutional matters.
 
• This is provided under Article 143 of the Constitution of India.
 
 
 
• **Certificate from High Court:**
 
 
• This refers to the process where a High Court certifies that a case involves a substantial question of law as to the interpretation of the Constitution, allowing it to be appealed directly to the Supreme Court.
 
• This is provided under Article 132 of the Constitution of India.

questions.question:
Which of the following statement/(s) is /are true with respect to Supreme Court Observation in A.G. Perarivalan vs The State Of Tamil Nadu State?

1. It highlighted that the Governor’s powers are qualified by the constitutional mandate, chiefly requiring them to act in aid and advice of the council of ministers

2. The bench headed by justice L Nageswara Rao ordered the freedom of one of the convicts in the Rajiv Gandhi assassination case.

3. The bench was of the opinion that there are three sources of power-Governor, Council of Ministers and the Constitution.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Both 1 and 2**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Governor's Powers:** The Supreme Court highlighted that the Governor's powers are qualified by the constitutional mandate, chiefly requiring them to act in aid and advice of the council of ministers.
 
• **Convict's Release:** The bench headed by Justice L Nageswara Rao ordered the freedom of one of the convicts in the Rajiv Gandhi assassination case.
 
• **Bench Composition:** The Supreme Court bench included Justice L Nageswara Rao and other justices who were instrumental in making the decision regarding the convict's release.
 
• **Constitutional Mandate:** The observations made by the Supreme Court emphasized the constitutional mandate that guides the Governor's actions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Governor's Role:**

 
 
• The Governor of a state in India acts as the nominal head, while the real powers of governance lie with the Chief Minister and the Council of Ministers.
 
• The Governor is appointed by the President of India and holds office at the President's pleasure.
 
• The Governor's actions and decisions are generally based on the advice of the Council of Ministers, except in certain exceptional situations where they may act at their discretion.
 
 
 
• **Rajiv Gandhi Assassination Case:**
 
 
• Rajiv Gandhi, the former Prime Minister of India, was assassinated on May 21, 1991, by a suicide bomber from the Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE).
 
• Several individuals were convicted in connection with the assassination, and the case has seen numerous legal proceedings over the years.
 
 
 
• **Supreme Court's Observations:**
 
 
• The Supreme Court's observations in this case underscore the importance of constitutional principles in guiding the actions of state authorities, including the Governor.
 
• The case highlights the delicate balance of power between the different branches of government and the role of the judiciary in upholding constitutional mandates.

questions.question: The Supreme Court, in May 2023, observed that it can give divorce on the ground of irretrievable breakdown of marriage by exercising its discretionary power under ________.

options.text: Article 142 of the Constitution of India
Article 136 of the Constitution of India
Article 143 of the Constitution of India
Article 32 of the Constitution of India

questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Article 142 of the Constitution of India**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In May 2023, the Supreme Court of India used Article 142(1) of the Indian Constitution to grant couples the right to divorce based on 'irretrievable breakdown of marriage'.
 
• Article 142(1) of the Indian Constitution reads, "The Supreme Court in the exercise of its jurisdiction may pass such decree or make such order as is necessary for doing complete justice in any cause or matter pending before it...".
 
• The Supreme Court's decision expanded the grounds on which divorce can be sought in India.
 
• Previously, the grounds for divorce were outlined in individual personal laws and did not include the concept of 'irretrievable breakdown of marriage' as it was not explicitly listed as grounds for divorce in any specific legislation. The 2023 ruling made it a valid reason to seek a divorce.
 
• The court used its discretionary powers to take cognizance of the realities of irreparable marriages and rule in favor of allowing legal terminations in such cases. This action sets a significant precedent for future cases involving such marital situations.
 
• This step by the Supreme Court could potentially pave the way for broader legal reform, rooting the law more firmly in the changing social context and conditions of the country.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 136 – Special Leave to Appeal to the Supreme Court****​**

 
 
• It Grants the Supreme Court discretionary power to allow special leave to appeal against any judgment, decree, or order in any cause or matter, passed by any court or tribunal.
 
• This article applies to both civil and criminal cases, giving broad powers to the Supreme Court to ensure justice.
 
• It cannot be used for appeals from judgments of military courts or tribunals.
 
 
 
• **Article 143 – Power of the President to Consult the Supreme Court**
 
 
• It Empowers the President of India to seek the advisory opinion of the Supreme Court on any question of law or fact of public importance.
 
• The Supreme Court's advice is not binding on the President; it is a consultative process.
 
• **It is ** Used to clarify constitutional or legal issues, like the Ayodhya case and the Berubari case.
 
 
 
• **Article 32** – **Right to Constitutional Remedies**
 
 
• **​It is one of the Fundamental Rights.**
 
• **It is the Heart and Soul of the Constitution.**
 
• It Empowers individuals to move the Supreme Court directly for the enforcement of fundamental rights guaranteed by the Constitution.

questions.question: A judge of the High Court retires at the age of ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**62**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The judge of High court retires at the age of 62.**
 
• According to Article 124(2) of the Constitution, the age of retirement for Supreme Court judges is **65**.
 
• As per Article 217(1) of the Constitution, **High Court judges** retire at **62**.
 
• Initially, the retirement age of High Court judges was 60, which was later in 1963 increased to 62 through the **15th constitutional amendment Bill**.
 
• The idea of increasing the age of **retirement** for judges has been mooted for decades as a solution for dealing with mounting pendency of cases and judicial vacancies. It has also been discussed in the context of ensuring serving judges do not look for post-retirement jobs from the executive.
 
• Attorney General for India **K K Venugopal** has been one of the vocal advocates of increasing tenure of the judges, and has consistently spoken about it at every farewell of Supreme Court judges since 2017.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The** High Courts** of India are the highest courts of appellate jurisdiction in each State and Union Territory of India.
 
• Judges in a high court are appointed by the **president of India** in consultation with the chief justice of India and the governor of the state under Art 217 of the Constitution but through subsequent judicial interpretations, the primacy of the appointment process is in the hands of the Judicial Collegium. High courts are headed by a chief justice.
 
• The chief justices rank **fourteenth** (within their respective states) and **seventeenth** (outside their respective states) on the Indian order of precedence.
 
• The number of judges in a court is decided by dividing the average institution of main cases during the last **five years** by the national average, or the average rate of disposal of main cases per judge per year in that high court, whichever is higher.

questions.question:
Which of the following statements are INCORRECT?

1) The Original Jurisdiction establishes the Supreme Court as an umpire in all disputes regarding federal matters.

2) The Supreme Court can give special orders in the form of writs.

3) Article 129 of the Indian Constitution mention about appointment of acting Chief Justice of India.

4) Every Judge of the Supreme Court of India shall be appointed by the Prime Minister of India.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**3 and 4**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Original Jurisdiction:** The Original Jurisdiction of the Supreme Court establishes it as an umpire in disputes regarding federal matters, such as disputes between different states or between the center and states. ***Hence, Statement 1 is correct.***
 
• **Writs by Supreme Court:** The Supreme Court can issue special orders in the form of writs for the enforcement of fundamental rights under Article 32 of the Indian Constitution. ***Hence, Statement 2 is correct.***
 
• **Article 129:** Article 129 of the Indian Constitution does not mention the appointment of an acting Chief Justice of India. Instead, it declares the Supreme Court to be a court of record. ***Hence, Statement 3 is incorrect.***
 
• **Appointment of Judges:** The appointment of Judges of the Supreme Court of India is done by the President of India as per Article 124 of the Indian Constitution, not by the Prime Minister. ***Hence, Statement 4 is incorrect.***

questions.question: In the case of Aparna Bhat vs State of Madhya Pradesh in 2021, the Supreme Court set aside the judgment of Madhya Pradesh High Court which prescribed ________ as condition for bail.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**tying** **rakhi**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ​In the case **Aparna Bhat vs. State of Madhya Pradesh**, the apex court held that the use of patriarchal and stereotypical reasoning/language which diminishes sexual crimes and tends to trivialize the survivor, is to be avoided under all circumstances.
 
• The** supreme court** was hearing an appeal against certain bail conditions within the case of Vikram vs State of Madhya Pradesh in Madhya Pradesh high court.
 
• In this case involving a sexual offence against a lady, the bench of Justice Rohit Arya ordered the bail for the accused on the condition that he visits the house of the complainant and requests her to tie the **Rakhi** band to him “with the promise to guard her to the most effective of his ability for all times to come back.” 
 
• While condemning the MP High Court’s order directing ‘**rakhi tying**’ as a condition for bail, the judgement explains the term ‘judicial stereotyping’, which refers to the practice of judges perpetuating harmful stereotypes, particularly for lady victims and survivors of violence.
 
• The Supreme Court put aside the judgment of Madhya Pradesh High Court which prescribed "**tying rakhi**" as condition for bail. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Supreme Court of India** is supreme judicial authority of India and is the highest court of the Republic of India under the constitution. 
 
• It is the** **most foremost senio**r** constitutional court, has the ultimate decision in all told legal matters, and also has the ability of judicial review except for Personal law board.
 
• The Supreme Court of India consist of the **Chief Justice** and **33 other Judges **appointed by the President of India.
 
• Supreme Court Judges retire upon attaining the age of **65 years**.
 
• After the retirement of **N. V. Ramana** who is the current Chief Justice of India, Justice** U. U. Lalit** will take oath as the New Chief Justice of India on 27th August 2022.

questions.question: According to the Constitution of India a Judge of the Supreme Court cannot be removed from office except by an order of the ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** **____**President**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **According to the Constitution of India, a Judge of the Supreme Court cannot be removed from office except by an order of the President**__.

 __
 
• A Judge of the Supreme Court shall not be removed from his office except by an order of the **President** passed after an address by each House of Parliament supported by a majority of the total membership of that House and by a majority of **not less than two - thirds **of the members of that House present and voting has been presented to the President in the same session for such removal on the ground of proved misbehaviour or incapacity.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Parliament may by law regulate the procedure for the presentation of an address and for the investigation and proof of the misbehaviour or incapacity of a Judge under **clause (4)**.

 
 
• Every person appointed to be a Judge of the Supreme Court shall, before he enters upon his office, make and subscribe before the President, or some person appointed in that behalf by him, an oath or affirmation according to the form set out for the purpose in the **Third Schedule.**
 
• No person who has held office as a Judge of the Supreme Court shall plead or act in any court or before any authority within the territory of India.

__
 
• The Supreme Court was set up in Calcutta by the East India Company in **1773.**__

• **King George – III **founded the Supreme Courts of Madras and Bombay on December 26, 1800, and December 8, 1823, respectively.
 
• The Constitution of India was enacted on **January 26, 1950**, after India gained independence in 1947.
 
• The Supreme Court of India was also established, with its inaugural meeting on** January 28, 1950**.
 
• The Supreme Court is established and constituted according to **Article 124.**
 
• The Supreme Court is the highest court in the country's judicial system.
 
• It is located in Tilak Marg,** New Delhi.**

questions.question: Which of the following organisations said that India CANNOT have a parallel judicial system - one for the rich and the other for the poor?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Supreme Court**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Supreme Court** of India emphasized that the country cannot have a parallel judicial system - one for the rich and the other for the poor.
 
• This statement underscores the importance of equality before the law and the need for a uniform judicial system that serves all citizens equally, regardless of their socio-economic status.
 
• The Supreme Court is the **highest judicial forum and final court of appeal under the Constitution of India**, and it has the power of judicial review.
 
• The Court's decision reflects its role in upholding the Constitution and ensuring justice is accessible to everyone.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Supreme Court of India** was established on **28th January 1950**, two days after the Constitution of India came into effect.
 
• It comprises the **Chief Justice of India and a maximum of 33 other judges**, appointed by the President of India.
 
• The Supreme Court's primary function is to interpret the Constitution and adjudicate disputes between the central government and state governments or between two or more states.
 
• The Court also has the authority to hear appeals against the judgments of lower courts and tribunals.
 
• Through its judgments, the Supreme Court plays a crucial role in the development of constitutional law and the protection of fundamental rights in India.

questions.question: Which Article of the Indian Constitution states that “Supreme Court to be a court of record”?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __Article 129.__

__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__

__
 
• Article 129

 
 
• ​Article 129 of the Indian Constitution empowers the Supreme Court to be a court of record.
 
• The Supreme Court shall have all the powers of such a court, including the power to punish for contempt of itself. 
 
• Court of Record is defined as
 
 
• a court whereof the acts and judicial proceedings are enrolled for a perpetual memorial and testimony
 
• which has the power to fine and imprison for contempt of its authority 
 
 
 
• Contempt of court signifies not only a willful disregard or disobedience of its orders, but such conduct as tends to bring the authority of the court.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__

 
• Article 135 was included in the Constitution to enable the Supreme Court to exercise jurisdiction in cases.
 
• Article 126 Appointment of acting Chief Justice – Constitution Of India
 
 
• When the office of Chief Justice of India is vacant, the duties of the office shall be performed by such one of the other Judges of the Court as the President may appoint for the purpose.
 
 
 
• The purpose behind Article 131 of the Indian Constitution is to uphold the spirit of cooperative federalism between the organs of the government.
 
• Under this Article, the Supreme Court has the original jurisdiction to adjudicate upon the matters of dispute between the states or between the center and state.

questions.question: Which of the following persons was appointed Chairman of the Second National Judicial Pay Commission?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Justice PV Reddi**__**.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Justice P.V. Reddi was appointed as the **Chairman of the Second National Judicial Pay Commission in 2010** to examine and recommend pay structures for judges in the higher judiciary.
 
• The Commission's primary objective was to assess the working conditions, remuneration, and **service conditions of judges**, including those in the **Supreme Court and High Courts**, to ensure adequate compensation and facilities.
 
• The Commission recommended significant **salary increases for judges**, including a proposal to enhance their salaries and pensions, addressing disparities compared to other services.
 
• The findings and recommendations of the Second National Judicial Pay Commission were crucial in **improving the morale and working conditions **of the judiciary, thus impacting the overall administration of justice in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Establishment:** The First National Judicial Pay Commission was established in 1996, and the Second NJPC was constituted in 2010.
 
• **Chairman:** The Second NJPC was chaired by Justice P.V. Reddi.
 
• The primary objective was to review and recommend pay scales, allowances, and service conditions for judges in the higher judiciary (Supreme Court and High Courts).
 
• **Salary Recommendations: **The Second NJPC recommended significant salary increases for judges, addressing disparities compared to other civil services.
 
• **Judicial Independence:** The NJPC aimed to enhance the independence of the judiciary by ensuring competitive compensation for judges.
 
• **Implementation:** The recommendations of the Second NJPC were implemented in 2016, leading to revised salary structures.
 
• **Impact on Judiciary: **The NJPC's recommendations improved the working conditions and morale of judges, thus positively impacting the administration of justice.
 
• **Pension Provisions: **The NJPC also addressed pension provisions for retired judges, ensuring financial security post-retirement.

questions.question: In February 2021, in the Devilal vs _______ case, the Supreme Court observed that juvenile offenders under 18 years and above 16 years are to be remitted to the jurisdictional Juvenile Justice Board.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**State of Madhya Pradesh.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__****Juvenile Justice And Its Procedure In India**

__
 
• The word juvenile originated from the** Latin word juvenis**, which means **young**.
 
• It means that a child has not completed the eighteenth year of age.
 
• The Supreme Court observed that juvenile offenders **under 18 years** and **above 16 years** are to be remitted to the jurisdictional Juvenile Justice Board.
 
• **Clause (l) of Section 2** of the **2000 Act** provides that “**juvenile in conflict with law**” means a “juvenile” who is alleged to have committed an offense and has not completed the eighteenth year of age as on the date of commission of such offense.
 
• **Section 20** also enables the court to consider and determine the juvenility of a person even after conviction by the regular court and also empowers the court, while maintaining the conviction.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Cabinet has approved amendments to the Juvenile Justice (**Care and Protection of Children**) **Act**, whereby juveniles in the age group of **16-18** can be tried under the** Indian Penal Code** (IPC) if they are accused of heinous crimes.
 
• Rejecting the recommendations of a Parliamentary Standing Committee, the Women and Child Development Ministry decided to go ahead with the proposal.
 
• The Supreme Court had also recently observed that there was a need to relook at the provisions of the Juvenile Justice Act in cases where the accused have committed crimes like** rape, murder dacoity and acid attacks**.
